# Large-library latency ceilings, measured 2026-10-13 on Windows amd64.
# Intel Core i7-13700H, 20 logical processors, NVMe, Go 1.27.2,
# CGO_ENABLED=1, CC=clang, no race detector. The fixture holds 100,000 photos.
# Five samples per figure, each the mean of three warmed calls (-benchtime=3x).
# One seed is shared across calls and no/folder/folder+tag+person blocks.
# Ranges below are the minimum and maximum of those five samples in ms/op.
# Events, EventsAfterCover, EventsRegroup and DuplicateGroupsRepeated were
# measured on 2026-10-14, when the event list began following its own journal.
# Things, People, DayBuckets, CountVisible, JobCountsDone and JobCountsPending
# were lowered on 2026-10-14, when those counts began to be kept in tables
# (migration 0037). The write calls' samples were retaken then, with their
# ceilings unchanged, to show what keeping the counts costs, except Ingest128:
# keeping the job counts adds a trigger to every queued job (about 35
# microseconds a photo), so its ceilings were raised by the rule below from
# those samples.
# LoadEmbeddings was added on 2026-10-15, with one 768-byte embedding for every
# photo in the seed.
# Every ceiling is max(5ms, 3 * slowest sample), rounded UP to one significant
# decimal digit. The 5ms floor keeps small timings from failing on ordinary noise.
# A ceiling catches substantial regressions; it is not a baseline or a 10% target.
# Raise a ceiling only by hand in review when an intentional feature/fixture
# change or repeat measurements on a supported machine justify the cost.
# Include the reason and at least five samples; investigate regressions first.
# Do not raise a ceiling simply to make a failing run pass. There is no --update.
# The gate also rejects a missing or unused budget. Names omit Go's CPU suffix.
# Table headroom is the extra latency allowed as a percentage of the figure:
# 100 * (budget / figure - 1).
# benchmark duration # measured minimum..maximum ms/op
BenchmarkLargeLibraryStore/none/Things 10ms # 2.672..3.170 ms/op
